newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu grapples with coalition, clashes.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu grapples with coalition, clashes.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failed to end weeks of coalition turmoil in a meeting on Wednesday with disgruntled Foreign Minister David Levy.
The crisis in the Israeli cabinet was overshadowed by the killing of a 16-year-old Palestinian in yet more violence in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Netanyahu held a 45-minute meeting with Foreign Minister David Levy in Jerusalem. Both sides said later nothing had been resolved.
"They had a serious meeting on the range of problems. The foreign minister heard the prime minister and made his remarks. Nothing has been finalised," Netanyahu's office said in a statement.
Levy, brooding for days for being left out of political decision-making, has threatened to resign over the way Netanyahu was running the government and Middle East peacemaking.
"The meeting we set has ended. We clarified the positions. The issues are serious and I have to determine my stand," Levy told reporters without elaborating.

Netanyahu was expected to assure Levy he would guide daily peacemaking with Palestinians, a process that has been deadlocked since the government sent in bulldozers last March to carve out a Jewish settlement on a hill in Arab East Jerusalem.
"He (Levy) will have to decide if he can continue being a partner in the government or not," said the head of Levy's five-member Gesher faction in parliament, Maxim Levy.
In the Gaza Strip, Israeli troops killed a Palestinian youth during a clash with Arab stone-throwers in a Jewish-Arab dispute over a strip of land near the Gush Katif settlement.
Soldiers in the West Bank town of Hebron, facing stones and petrol bombs thrown by Arab protesters, fired live ammunition and rubber bullets wounding 26 Palestinians.

Witnesses said Israeli snipers deployed across rooftops and alleyways along the dividing line between Israeli- and PLO-controlled sectors of Hebron. Arab shops were shuttered in a general strike called to protest anti-Moslem posters depicting the Prophet Mohammed as a pig.
"A war is being waged in Hebron and they're bickering. It's a mockery," said legislator Uzi Baram of the main opposition Labour party, referring to the feud between Levy and Netanyahu.
Levy's resignation threat was triggered by the disclosure on Friday that cabinet minister Ariel Sharon met last month with top PLO official Mahmoud Abbas without the foreign minister's knowledge.
The quarrel came on the heels of a parliamentary no-confidence vote in which 11 coalition members were either absent or failed to support Netanyahu in anger at what they view as mismanagement.

"I don't think there will be an end to the turmoil in Netanyahu's government until he gains the confidence of more of the public by changing the way he runs his office," said political analyst Chemi Shalev of the daily Maariv newspaper.
"If he repeats his mistakes, his government will eventually fall," he told Reuters.
